what: Add a PIN per profile on this device.
why: Four other clients have one. The owner decided it ships with the TV shell's account picker; until then "Stay signed in" off is the privacy control. It needs a decision record.

what: Offer the same three skip modes for Recap, Preview and Commercial segments.
why: Jellyfin marks these segment types besides Intro and Outro; skipping them follows the same pattern as Skip intro.

what: Ask "Still watching?" after several episodes play in a row.
why: A prompt like other services use; it stops a series from playing all night.

what: Add an audio sync offset control to the player.
why: Viewers fix lip-sync problems with a per-title offset; it needs a typed player command.

what: Show two subtitle tracks at once (dual subtitles).
why: Dual subtitles have 134 likes on Infuse's forum and 93 thumbs-up across three Jellyfin clients. Subtitle timing (T12-04) is a different control. It needs a typed player command.

what: Run a compatibility test pass against Jellyscale across sign-in, browse, and the routes a Netflix-like UI needs.
why: Octave assumes Jellyscale provides the APIs needed to stream, with no audit yet. Stubs at the time: /Items/{id}/Similar, /Genres, /Persons, /Items/{id}/LocalTrailers, /Items/Filters2, /Shows/NextUp (Next up row empty), /Search/Hints (404), likes and ratings (404), /Items/Suggestions (mixed). Not built: Quick Connect, user management, trickplay, media segments, library and metadata work. Fixes are separate tasks.

what: Check whether a client can offer a watchlist on Jellyfin 10.11 or 12.x.
why: A watchlist is a top-voted Jellyfin request; whether a client can do it is unverified. The owner let Favorites stand in for a watchlist (2026-11-12). Removing an item from Continue watching is task T5-05.

what: Make new library items appear without a restart.
why: The server sends LibraryChanged on its socket; Octave handles UserDataChanged only, so a new title shows after a restart.

what: Design a "server unreachable" state for browsing, with a way back when the server returns.
why: Browsing offline shows plain errors; the viewer needs to know the cause and see the screen recover on its own.

what: Add playlists.
why: Smart playlists have 1,425 votes on Plex and 588 on Jellyfin. They are a server feature; a remembered filter is the client-side part. Extras, trailers and genre pages are covered by T12-08.

what: Remember a library's filters between visits.
why: The sort is covered by T6-03; remembering filters between visits has no task.

what: Hide filter chips a library cannot match (using /Items/Filters2).
why: A chip that always returns nothing wastes a press.

what: Translate the app.
why: Every string is English only. Needs a string table and a decision on which languages.

what: Add a private session that plays without reporting, for watching on someone else's account.
why: Useful on a shared TV. Anonymous or guest access has 88 votes on Jellyfin's tracker. Touches Playstate Reporting (ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.2).

what: After the credits finish, offer "More like this" in an end-of-film card, never over the credits.
why: Keeps the viewer watching without cutting the credits. Needs a More like this row.

what: Use the time of day and the runtime to rank suggestions.
why: Evening suggestions fit a shorter film. Needs a viewer profile.

what: Let the viewer reorder or hide Home rows.
why: 47% of 3,000 surveyed viewers would absolutely use hiding rows they do not use. The owner chose a fixed order for now.

what: Revisit genre rows on Home after the dogfood week.
why: The case against them was an inference, not evidence; 82% of 1,362 subscribers said in 2020 that they would use groupings of similar content (intent).

what: Add a Home row for a collection.
why: Collections are a natural row for a franchise the viewer is part way through.

what: Ask Jellyscale to implement POST /Sessions/Capabilities and /Sessions/Capabilities/Full.
why: They are stubs there at the time of writing, so a phone cannot control Octave through Jellyscale (T12-06). Media segments, Quick Connect and trickplay, the other items of the carry-over list, are T10-10, T10-06 and T10-11.
source: owner, 2026-11-12 (loves D8 A); status from the Jellyscale compat table

what: Add a Favorites row on Home.
why: A pinned watch list came second of 13 features in a survey of 3,000; Favorites stands in for the watch list.

what: Add a "Watched" view of finished titles, newest first.
why: 835 votes on Jellyfin's tracker; no usage data. The owner chose not for now.

what: Let the viewer mark a suggested title "Not this one".
why: Where the dismissal is kept is the open question; the owner chose to wait for the server-side profile.

what: Prepare the next episode during the Up Next countdown, direct play only.
why: 223 votes. Decide after the gap between episodes is measured. Touches Playback Negotiation.

what: Let a phone running any Jellyfin app act as the remote and keyboard.
why: Third of 13 features in the same survey of 3,000.

what: Lead the mobile task list with offline downloads when that list is written.
why: The most-voted Jellyfin client request (1,827 votes). A note for planning mobile.

what: Mark cards for what is new since the last visit.
why: Netflix added status tags in 2025; no usage data found.

what: Add picture-in-picture.
why: No usage data was found for it. A sleep timer is a separate entry, and a dialogue-boost option folds into the clear-voices entry.

what: Show captions for the stretch a viewer skips back over, and resume 3 s early.
why: Owner decision D2 B. Captions on skip-back are on by default, which most platforms do not do; check in the dogfood week and change the default if it surprises.

what: Add a sleep timer with "Stop after this episode".
why: Weak evidence; the owner kept it here (D4 A). It replaces the sleep-timer part of the loves entry.

what: Show "Where you left off" on the series page after a long gap.
why: The owner kept it here (D8 A); no demand evidence.

what: Add a cast strip to the paused player.
why: 39 votes on Jellyfin's tracker; the owner kept it here (D10 A).

what: Limit the overview under the focused episode card to two lines in DESIGN.md.
why: DESIGN.md gives no line limit for it; two lines matches the owner's "very succinct" condition.

what: Revisit whether settings follow the account across clients.
why: "Global defaults across clients" has 260 votes, and Jellyfin and Jellyscale both keep a per-account preferences record. T9-01 decides which settings follow the account.

what: Seek further with a held key, and jump by chapter.
why: Owner decision D5 B. A held remote key should speed up the seek.

what: Decide whether the TV form gets recent searches, per account, with a Clear control.
why: Shows what was searched to the next person at the screen. Decide with the TV shell.

what: Add a letter jump in a library sorted by name.
why: No evidence either way. Decide with the TV shell.

what: Add a subtitle size control before subtitle styling ships.
why: Decide after the first dogfood evening. Bringing one control forward needs a typed player command. The BBC sizes subtitles at 7 to 8% of picture height in at most two lines; a US device rule lists size from 50% to 200%, colour, background and edge style.

what: Check the TV platform rules in the screen specs: no dependence on a Menu key, no exit confirmation, and a per-platform safe inset.
why: Android TV's quality rules say not to depend on a Menu key or confirm exit; tvOS wants 60 pt top and bottom where --safe-y is 54 px, and Roku wants more for text. Season tabs wrap at their ends and rows stop.

what: Measure the time from a key press to focus moving, check --void and --surface-0 for banding on a real panel, and check windowing for a library grid.
why: One service halved key-to-focus time and card views doubled it; a library grid renders every loaded card with no windowing.

what: Add a DESIGN.md section 11 rule that every slider has a spoken value.
why: The audit's A11. The scrubber and the volume slider are covered; the rule's wording waits for the owner.

what: Add row hints for a screen reader on TV ("row 2 of 5, Continue watching").
why: Do it after the screen-reader audit.

what: Add a check that fails on a source file over about 400 lines.
why: WORKFLOW.md still lists it under mechanical enforcement; the code-quality review found large files (gateway.ts at 955 lines).

what: Drop the typescript-6 alias, scripts/typescript-6-resolve.mjs and the Dependabot ignore once dependency-cruiser and typescript-eslint support the app's TypeScript 7 minor.
why: The alias also serves @typescript-eslint/parser (peer typescript below 6.1.0 at 8.72.2); .github/dependabot.yml still ignores typescript-6. Whether the ignore applies is unverified.

what: Make scripts/lint-boundaries.mjs exit 1 for any violation count.
why: It passes the violation count as the exit code (process.exit(exitCode)), so exactly 256 violations exit 0. Use exitCode > 0 ? 1 : 0.

what: Make the account reset safe for a second user on the same gateway.
why: The reset runs only when the gateway object changes. A "Who's watching?" switch that logs in another user on the same gateway would skip it; document that a gateway is single-user or key the drop on the user id.

what: Record nextUpDateCutoff for a series that gains a whole new season.
why: The recorder covered only a new episode in an existing season.

what: Follow POST /Collections?ids= with POST /Collections/{id}/Items in any collection-creating code.
why: On Jellyfin 12.4.0 the first call creates an empty collection. Re-check on newer 12.x images.

what: Join collections client-side on Jellyfin 10.11 for the sequel rule.
why: 10.11.7 has no GET /Items/{itemId}/Collections (404), so Home's sequel rule is skipped there and the hero falls to Similar. List collections and fetch each one's members until the finished film is found (up to N + 1 extra requests on an empty-row Home), and record one more fixture.

what: Make the recorders' numbered id-N fakes stable across recordings.
why: Seed them in a fixed order and keep one scrubber (makeSave() in record-discovery-fixtures.mjs resets the counter mid-recording), so a re-record diffs cleanly.

what: Check whether Jellyfin's NFO reader skips season and episode numbers for an episode added under a series with lockdata.
why: Seen in the fixture servers; unverified elsewhere. Octave's own library tests may meet the same.

what: Add a Path allow-list (/media/) to the fixture scrubbing test.
why: tests/fixtures/jellyfin/*/discovery-suggestions.json, discovery-local-trailers.json and discovery-special-features.json keep the CI container's sample paths.

what: Diff field shapes, not names and counts, in docs/research/discovery-api.md section 1 rows marked "Same.".
why: A later gateway task must not rely on identical fields across versions without a diff.

what: Re-run tests/integration/record-fixtures.mjs against both servers to confirm it still records.
why: It was refactored onto fixture-recording.mjs and checked only with node --check.

what: Match the saver's credential pattern in the discovery fixtures test.
why: src/lib/jellyfin/discovery-fixtures.test.ts scans credentials with a weaker pattern than fixture-recording.mjs: use the i flag and (?:=|%3D).

what: Guard the cleanup in record-discovery-fixtures.mjs.
why: The finally block calls waitFor unguarded and the final resetUser() sits outside any finally; a killed run leaves a staged episode file and watch state. Remove a leftover copy at recorder start.

what: Ask Jellyscale for a partial update of the user configuration, or a version check that refuses a stale save.
why: POST /Users/Configuration replaces the whole object, so two apps saving at once can overwrite each other; a fresh read narrows the window but cannot close it. Asked in an Octave issue comment; not yet filed in Jellyscale's tracker.

what: Ask Jellyscale for a published, versioned image and the Babel Film fixture in a form Octave's CI can fetch or generate.
why: scripts/generate-samples.sh cannot make the PGS track, because ffmpeg cannot encode PGS. Not yet filed.

what: Redact a secret with no digit and under 20 characters after a space.
why: safeReason and redactText leave "password hunter" unchanged; redacting it would also redact "token expired".

what: Reduce over-redaction in the text filters.
why: "Invalid token (401)" becomes "Invalid token [redacted]", and any word:NNNN or word:NNNNN becomes [address] (pts:12345, bitrate:8000). A single-label host with a one- to three-digit port (nas:80) stays visible.

what: Make safeReason hide a bare host or IP address with no port, and a path after a colon with no space.
why: "open failed:/home/u/x" is shown unchanged (src/lib/safe-reason.ts).

what: Hide IPv6 zone-id addresses and a scheme-less user:pass@host in safeReason.
why: "connect [fe80::1%eth0]:8096 failed" is unchanged, a bare fe80::1%eth0:8096 becomes fe80::1%[address], and user:pass@host:8096 becomes user:pass@[address], still showing the credential.

what: Hide a whole path that contains a space in safeReason.
why: "cannot open /home/u/My Movie.mkv now" becomes "cannot open [path] Movie.mkv now" and c:\Program Files\x becomes [path] Files\x, so filename fragments reach the screen.

what: Split scripts/generate-samples.sh (about 470 lines) by sample family.
why: Movies, shows, staging and verify in separate scripts keep CI's sample step readable.

what: Make the fixture recorders reproduce the committed fixtures on a fresh server.
why: Numbered id-N values, online-matched titles and DateCreated differ even between two runs in a row (the staged episode's DateCreated, and the HEVC film's title in discovery-suggestions). Lock the HEVC sample with an NFO or normalize the dates in the scrubber.

what: Give each recorder login its own device id, or note the limit in tests/integration/.
why: The recorders log a user in on a fixed device id, so a second login as the same user ends the first token (seen when the language recorder logged a user in twice).

what: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 that OriginalLanguage gives the file's default audio track on plain Jellyfin and that a ger preference matches audio tagged deu.
why: Recorded on both servers (A2); ARCHITECTURE.md does not say it today.

what: Mark hearing-impaired tracks in the detail labels.
why: SubtitleInfo has no hearing-impaired flag, so such tracks match by language and read like any other. The player's two-line labels already say "hard of hearing".

what: Add a test for a failed /Localization/Cultures read in src/lib/jellyfin/account-languages.ts.
why: No test covers it.

what: Add a "no matching track" cell to the account-language recorder, for audio and subtitles.
why: Cover a chosen language the file lacks, PlayDefaultAudioTrack false with no language, and Smart or Always with no language. Settings shows those reads as "Set in another Jellyfin app" until recorded.

what: Add page-wise jumps (PageUp and PageDown, or letter rows) to the TV Picker sheet.
why: The language list has 486 entries on 12.4.0, and the subtitle list can be doubled.

what: Set defaultAudioStreamIndex to the source's flagged default track when a direct-played pick is not an embedded track.
why: The plan echoes the pick (fixtures show DefaultAudioStreamIndex: 2 for pick 2), so the player falls back to its own choice, not necessarily the file's flagged default that the notice names.

what: Add a Settings sheet to the player.
why: The owner asked to change a client setting without leaving playback. A change that affects the stream refreshes it and resumes at the same position, keeping the audio and subtitle tracks (the streaming-limit renegotiation path already does this). Open questions: which settings, how the sheet opens with a remote, what the viewer sees during a refresh, and whether a language change also switches the playing tracks.

what: Add personal ratings: rate a title, a Top rated view, and a Home row.
why: The owner decided on 2026-11-19: half stars, rate on the title page then a prompt when a film ends, 4 stars and up. Jellyfin stores a per-user 0 to 10 Rating; the server has no sort or threshold filter by it, so Octave computes the lists from one request. DELETE /UserItems/{id}/Rating is the only call that clears a rating. The viewer's own rating sits apart from audience and critic scores. API facts are in tests/fixtures/jellyfin/README.md (Personal ratings).
source: owner request, 2026-11-17; desktop tasks P16-14 to P16-17

what: Check whether a renegotiation keeps a paused title paused, and whether direct play after a renegotiation selects the kept subtitle track.

why: T2-06 review low: the rule appears only in §3, so a T8-08 reader of §2 could miss the host refusal.

what: Check that the app bundler (Metro/Hermes) can import packages/core/tests/fixtures/*.json for runUrlConformance on a device.
why: T2-06 review low: only Node import is tested; the fixture path lies outside the package source root.

what: Run the Jellyscale fixture from the published image pinned by digest once it can be pulled anonymously.
why: T2-08: the base images inside a commit build (golang, alpine, the ffmpeg package) can move, and a cold build costs CI time. The GHCR package answered 401 to an anonymous pull on 2026-11-21.

what: Bring Jellyscale's Babel Film (PGS and many-language tracks) into Octave's fixture, or a sample Octave can generate.
why: T2-08: backlog entry 64 asked for it. T2-08 runs Octave's own samples, ffmpeg cannot encode PGS, and Jellyscale's -fixtures image is not pullable.

what: Ask Jellyscale for a way to create a non-admin user and a user who may not convert. Not yet filed.
why: T2-08: setup can make only the admin on Jellyscale, so T2-09 cannot check the conversion-not-allowed refusal or keep discovery state apart there.

what: Ask Jellyscale for /Items/{id}/Collections. Not yet filed.
why: T2-08 recorded it as a stub (200 from a declared stub at b920b193cd6f), and the detail page's collection row calls it.

what: Give each checkout its own Compose project name: tests/integration/docker-compose.yml derives the project 'integration' from its directory, so parallel worktrees collide and a run can orphan another's servers.
why: T2-08: an orphaned 'integration' project from a deleted checkout held ports 18096/18097 and blocked the three-server run until the owner removed it.

what: Refine the TV browse rows' look on F4 with a row draw distance of about 150: the lift that does not animate, 16-bit artwork, the 1280 px backdrop, and no in-memory image cache, each changed and measured on the Shield against the memory and frame targets.
why: The owner chose F4 with a row draw distance of about 150 on 2026-11-21 and asked for the look to be refined later in a measured follow-up; F1 kept the lift but measured 328 MB, over the target.

what: Do not read HDR in the direct-play decision: a Dolby Vision profile 5 file on a display without it direct-plays today.
why: The capability list's hdr field is not read by devicePlayability (T2-07), so HDR and Dolby Vision support never forces the conversion.

what: Judge a first-answer conversion, and a disc's forced fallback, against the device: either can copy a codec the device cannot decode.
why: T2-07 only asks again when the server offers direct play; a TranscodingUrl from the first request or the disc path is used as the server built it.

what: Judge audio tracks other than the chosen one, channel counts, levels and frame rates in devicePlayability.
why: T2-07 reads only the first video stream and the one judged audio stream, so a device limit on anything else is not seen.

what: Keep video stream copy when only the audio cannot play (the forced request turns both off today).
why: T2-07 D8: acceptance item 2 and the 2026-11-20 amendment send AllowVideoStreamCopy false whatever the cause, so a playable video is re-encoded for an audio-only problem. Needs a Product Owner ruling on the amendment.

what: Add the T2-07 device-conversion answers to hls-master-urls.json as shared HLS vectors before T8-08.
why: The file is frozen; the new answers are not vectors yet, so a native validator never sees a forced-conversion master URL. Needs a Product Owner ruling.

what: Fail the app's composition when no DeviceCapabilitySource is passed to JellyfinGateway (T8-07).
why: T2-07 D2: the default is full, so an app that forgets the source direct-plays everything and the engine fails with decoder-unavailable.

what: Check that the device can play what the forced conversion produces, and that the server really re-encodes.
why: T2-07: the first forced-answer row accepts any URL with stream copy off. A failed probe, a list without h264 or aac, or a source above a decoder's size limit still gets a plan the device may not decode. Unverified, recalled Jellyfin behaviour: a server with HEVC or AV1 encoding enabled may re-encode into the source's own codec, since the profile's VideoCodec list holds it. T2-09 expects the conversion, so this does not block.

what: Tell the viewer when their audio pick is dropped because the device cannot play that track and the original plays with the default audio.
why: T2-07: the settled rule 'a pick never costs a direct play' wins, and the plan reports the source's default audio with no notice (the drop of a non-embedded pick has one). The owner decides the copy; none is invented here.

what: Decide what the probe reports as a decoder profile: strict profile matching converts a source with no Profile when every decoder states one.
why: T2-07 devicePlayability refuses a source whose Profile is missing when a decoder states one (T8-07 decides what its probe reports).

what: The T8-07 probe must list every supported profile of a decoder as its own VideoDecoder entry, or leave the profile out when the decoder plays any.
why: T2-07 review: devicePlayability matches a stated profile exactly (device-capabilities.ts). A probe that lists only the top profile (h264 High, hevc Main 10) makes an 8-bit HEVC Main or an h264 Main source force a server conversion of a file the device plays. The port's comment on VideoDecoder.profile now states the rule.

what: Let the play-method check find a session on Jellyscale.
why: T2-09 milestone 1 confirmed: Jellyscale's /Sessions PlayState has no MediaSourceId, which the core matches on, so gateway.sessionPlayMethod never answers there and the app cannot tell copy from encode. The tripwire pins this as unanswered. Not yet filed.

what: Record the forced-conversion answer for the AV1 sample on both Jellyfin servers.
why: T2-09 checks it live only (the no-av1 set); T2-07 recorded the H.264 and HEVC answers.

what: Give the on-device tripwire (T8-20) a way to read tests/integration/tripwire-expectations.ts.
why: The expectation table is TypeScript under tests/, and a Kotlin run needs to read the same rows.

what: Make Jellyscale's item list carry every audio stream of a media source.
why: T2-09: GET /Items with Fields=MediaSources returns one audio stream for the multitrack film, while GET /Items/{id} returns both; the tripwire reads the detail for its audio-pick sample. Not yet filed.

what: Decide what the app should say when a Blu-ray folder's main file is listed as a plain film.
why: T2-09: Jellyscale lists the folder's BDMV/STREAM .m2ts as one film, and the core's disc-path rule refuses it as disc-source after a forced second request, so the viewer sees a refusal for a file Jellyscale could have served. The owner decides the behaviour.
